raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
PP previously returned each microbatch parameter gradient to Python for accumulation.

Use one accumulating graph per PP backward path and stage. The first executed backward for each stage in a step zeroes its persistent accumulators; every full, split-dW, and multiplexed backward updates and returns the same handles; REDUCE_GRAD consumes the final handles once.

With the shared add-chain support from #5119, supported WGrad producers fuse into the accumulator when enabled. Unsupported producers retain explicit add_.

Validation: 90 focused WGrad and GraphPP runtime tests passed.

nodes.body:
This is doubling the number of graph we need to worry about. 
and it's for per-stage... every bw stage have 2 versions... 

I wonder if the perf gain is really worth it. 
The alternative is to just use one graph, and always do gradient accumulation for mb0. My bet is that it would matter less than 1% for E2E.

thanks, this is much simpler than the 2 graph variant. 

I wonder if we should do the same for spmd with ga case, i.e. make the first mb graph just take gradient buffer as input, and do the redundant accumulate into zero for mb0. 

There will be a perf hit, but is simpler.
